source_review.notes: Checked current ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148:2018 and 15288:2023 metadata and the ISO online browsing entry; NASA Technical Requirements Definition and requirement-writing appendix; SEBoK 2.14 System Requirements Definition; INCOSE Guide for Writing Requirements version 4 preview metadata; and the Mavin et al. EARS DOI. NASA and SEBoK returned HTTP 200, and the DOI resolver returned HTTP 202. ISO and INCOSE returned HTTP 403 to the command-line client; their current metadata/content was independently inspected during authoring, but command-line reachability is not claimed.

evidence: Reviewed the functional-requirement tuple, condition-subject-modal-behavior grammar, source and need-coverage predicates, black-box state transition, trace-rationale relation, verification relation, readiness predicate, and overlapping-transition conflict condition.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Every symbol is introduced before use. Needs, operational statements, functions, performance, quality, interfaces, constraints, architecture, procedures, verification, and validation remain distinct.

evidence: Executed functional-requirement-record-check under Python 3.14.4 and independently recomputed five records, one well-formed declared record, missing source FR-004, missing trigger and verification FR-003, weak verb FR-002:support, and compound signal FR-005:and.
numerical_recomputation.notes: The checker is exact for declared fields and its four-word lexical list only; it does not establish semantic atomicity, necessity, feasibility, correct system boundary, or set completeness.

evidence: Re-derived the source obligation for every functional requirement and the need-coverage-or-justified-gap obligation for every baselined need.
Checked the conditional state-transition representation and demonstrated how incompatible next states under overlapping state/event/guard conditions expose a requirement-set conflict.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The predicates are review disciplines, not proofs of correct interpretation, completeness, feasibility, safety, or implementation conformance.

evidence: Reviewed wrong-level subjects, affected non-users, operator-versus-system obligations, invalid/stale/duplicate/conflicting input, concurrency, timeout, interruption, cancellation, degraded dependencies, initialization, maintenance, update, emergency, retirement, security threats, safety prohibitions, clinical AI, and grid-connected physical operation.

Challenged all ten examples and five answers for design leakage, false atomicity, vague verbs, hidden performance, orphan derivation, happy-path bias, unobservable end states, and unsupported domain authority.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: High-consequence functions remain conditional on applicable domain, safety, security, human-factors, regulatory, and independent evidence; no such external review is claimed.

evidence: Traced obligation, source, observable-behavior, condition/exception, and closure invariants through exposition, ten worked examples, and five complete answers.
Verified that every candidate construction distinguishes normative text from rationale, metadata, performance, design, procedure, and verification method.
invariant_checking.notes: Set-level review includes source and operational-thread coverage, state consistency, producer/consumer closure, feasibility, traceability, and a plausible verification path.

proof_review.notes: The chapter presents conditional relations and review predicates but no theorem proof.

proof_sketch_labeling.notes: No passage is presented as a proof sketch.

evidence: Reviewed uses of prove, evidence, verify, validate, necessary, feasible, atomic, complete, safe, secure, clinical, compliant, and correct.
artifacts/snippets/SYSENG-013/report.json records exact local execution evidence for declared fields and lexical signals.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: Execution establishes record-shape and bounded lexical observations only. It cannot establish semantic requirement quality, functional coverage, system safety, security adequacy, clinical benefit, regulatory conformity, or external review.

conceptual_review.notes: Professor-style review checked requirement, function, system of interest, source, derived requirement, trigger, precondition, guard, response, postcondition, atomicity, state transition, functional chain, performance, quality, interface, constraint, architecture, verification, and validation for conceptual consistency.

practitioner_review.notes: Practitioner-style review checked public warning, payment refunds, transit gates, emergency location, duplicate commands, medical-pump interlocks, identity conflict, export cancellation, warehouse allocation, emergency shutdown, clinical triage, account recovery, railway doors, and home energy control. Each example exposes assumptions, intermediate reasoning, evidence limits, and bounded conclusions. Internal practitioner-oriented review only.

pedagogical_review.notes: Pedagogical review confirmed progression from obligation boundary and source transformation through black-box behavior, normative grammar, conditions, inputs/outputs, exceptions, state and flow models, derived requirements, attributes, individual/set review, verification planning, and stakeholder validation. Ten examples and five complete answers require classification, rewriting, derivation, comparison, and high-consequence transfer.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external academic or practitioner review is claimed.
